summary.title: Questions to ask your interviewer
summary.one_liner: Learn which specific, hard-to-dodge questions reveal a company's real engineering process, culture and feedback habits during a job interview.
keywords: red flags in a job interview
takeaways: Ask specific or drill-down questions rather than general ones like 'Do you trust management?', which invite white lies.
Watch for red flags: manual deployments, missing tests or code review, and interviewers who can't give real examples.
Ask how often engineers are pulled off their primary task and what the role really involves.
Probe culture with questions on decision-making, what it takes to succeed beyond 'hard work', and how performance feedback works.
Ask how you will grow (training, mentoring, conferences); a vague answer suggests you'll be left on your own.
summary.summary: The author, continuing an earlier post on designing technical interviews as a filter, argues that candidates should question companies too, since job-seeking engineers get little reliable information before interviews. The article explains why general questions get polished or dishonest answers and recommends concrete, drill-down questions instead. It groups example questions into red flags, technical (development and deployment process, communication tools), and culture (decision-making, success criteria, feedback, growth), with commentary on what good and bad answers look like. The tone is opinionated and anecdotal, drawing on the author's and friends' experiences.
